title: The legacy criteria of RWB-E4-045 are generic, the split gives this slice only AC2, and the slice carries no requirement id
source: Legacy RWB-E4-045 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.5.4.1 (AC-P8-005-01) and A2.5.4.3; work package line for RWB-P8-E4045-APP (acs AC2, reqs empty)
description: The key owns two criteria and both are generic. AC1 reads 'Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives / Then works out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data / Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version' and AC2 reads 'Given the decision log cannot be written / When the action is taken / Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003'. The split plan gives AC2 to this application story and AC1 to RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG, so the calculation this story builds has no criterion of its own, and the four legacy test cases repeat the two rows without a case, a fee type, an amount or a date. The FSD main success criterion AC-P8-005-01 is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead' and the FSD 'Requirements served' table of P8 is empty, so the module adds no value either. The story therefore keeps AC2 word for word, states its own synthetic fee set for the test cases, and traces the calculation to FEAT-PAY-05 and AC-P8-005-01.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-045 AC1 and AC2 as quoted; legacy test cases TC-E4-045-01 'Calculate fees and charges' and TC-E4-045-02 'Not recorded' with no data column; FSD P8 v3 A2.5.4.1 AC-P8-005-01 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version / Written one epic ahead'; split plan rows RWB-P8-E4045-APP (acs AC2) and RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG (acs AC1).
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the Payment module owner
proposed: Publish the fee facts of FEAT-PAY-05 as a documented example set in FSD P8 in its next version, so that the application and the integration story of the key assert against one set of rows instead of a stated synthetic one.

title: The fee tables held as data have no owning service and no place in this schema, and the consumed reads that carry them are unpublished
source: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.1 and A2.5.2; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (proceeds, payment_match_rule only) and T5.2; context pack P8 ownership rows (tables: proceeds; two provided operations, no consumed one); Template and Rules R3 default ruling on parameters and reference data
description: The feature works the amount out 'from the fee tables held as data', and no source says who owns those tables or where they live. The ownership map gives this service one table, proceeds, and the TSD declares only proceeds and payment_match_rule, so no fee table can be written in rwb_payment. The rows the calculation reads are therefore another owner's versioned data: reference data and parameters are ruled to rwb-case by the default ruling of Template and Rules R3, and the partner facts the legacy data table names are rwb-partner's. None of those read operations is published: the module appendix lists the two provided operations only and the context pack confirms that P8 owns no consumed operation. The story carries every read as a placeholder with its owning service and its path base, declares no fee table, and builds against the fakes until the names are published.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.1 'Works out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data'; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 lists proceeds and payment_match_rule and no fee table; context pack P8 'Tables (1) proceeds' and 'REST operations provided (2)' with no consumed section; Template and Rules R3 'Parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) | P3 rwb-case'.
owner_role: P8 data owner, the P3 reference-data owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Name the owner of the fee tables in the Ownership Map and the Logical Data Model, publish the read that returns a fee row with its version, and state in TSD P8 T3.1 whether any fee row is stored in rwb_payment; the placeholders and the fakes of the story are then replaced by the published names.

title: No fee type list, fee row value, rate, cap or fee-specific message is published, and rule_row is named by the legacy key but is not the source of the value
source: Legacy RWB-E4-045 (Data table: rule_row DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015; Validation and messages); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (no fee table) and T3.2 (LOV-MATCH includes FEE); FSD P8 v3 A2.5.3.1 (VR-P8-005-1, BR-P8-005); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42, R-DIS-10, R-DIS-54, R-DIS-64, R-WO-37
description: The calculation must state what it reads and what it records, and no source publishes it. There is no list of fee types, no fee row, no rate, no flat amount, no cap and no validity anywhere in the FSD, the TSD or the routing logic; LOV-MATCH offers FEE as a match target and nothing more. The legacy data table names rule_row, the rule table of rwb-decision, while the feature is specified as fee tables held as data, so the story records the fee row identity and its version instead of a rule ID, and reads no rule package at all (DP-04 is not applied). No message is published for a fee type with no row in force, so that condition is carried as a placeholder. The story therefore treats every value as a row read at run time, puts no value in code, and holds no copy of any fee or rule table.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.3.1 BR-P8-005 'No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version'; TSD P8 v2 T3.2 'LOV-MATCH INSTALLMENT, SETTLEMENT, FEE, SALE_PROCEEDS, UNMATCHED' with no fee type list; legacy RWB-E4-045 Data table row rule_row DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 and Validation and messages MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 only.
owner_role: the reference-data owner (P3), the P7 rule owner and the P8 business analyst
proposed: Publish the fee type list and the fee rows with their rate, cap, validity and version, and add the message for a fee type with no row in force, so that the story asserts against documented values instead of a stated reading.

title: The service owns no fee operation and no fee event, so the answer of the calculation has no published carrier
source: Context pack P8 (REST operations provided: GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match; events EV-11, EV-12, EV-25); TSD P8 v2 T5.3 and T-A.1; FSD P8 v3 A2.5.2 and A2.5.4.4
description: The feature is a system step that runs unattended, and nothing in the target carries its answer across a service boundary. The service provides two operations, both on proceeds, and owns three events, TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched; no fee operation and no fee event exists in the ownership map, the TSD event table or the FSD. A route owner that needs a fee, and the approver who signs it off, therefore cannot ask for it or receive it on a published contract. The story keeps the answer inside the service: the local decision record of DP-03 carries the calculation and the proceeds row with matched_to FEE carries the money side, and the story declares no operation, no topic and no event name of its own.
evidence: Context pack P8 'REST operations provided (2) GET /proceeds, POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match' and 'Events (3) EV-11, EV-12, EV-25'; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 'TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed, ProceedsMatched' all published; FSD P8 v3 A2.5.2 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' with no answer path.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the service contract owner
proposed: Publish either a fee operation or a FeeCalculated event on rwb.payment.events.v1 with its CloudEvents envelope and its key, and add the ownership row; the carrier is then declared in the contract baseline of the service and the cross-service journey can assert it.

title: The fee run and its activity have no published names, and the trigger of the calculation is stated two different ways
source: Context pack P8 (Jobs JOB-07 and JOB-08; Workflows 0); FSD P8 v3 A2.5.2 step 1 and A2.5.4.4 (AC-BG-P8-005-01); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 FEE_DUE, WORK_ORDER_RAISED, BROKER_SOLD, PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF
description: The slice needs one run and one activity, and no source names either: the context pack lists the two jobs of the service and zero workflows, and no document names the fee run. The trigger is stated two ways. The FSD says the step 'receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', and its background row AC-BG-P8-005-01 repeats the module boilerplate 'ACE batch for source ALS complete / Daily', while the routing logic makes a fee fall due on a stage event of four different routes (FEE_DUE, WORK_ORDER_RAISED, BROKER_SOLD, PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF). Nothing states whether the run is event-started or a child of the case workflow, and nothing names the activity. The story declares one event-started workflow per fee fact on queue rwb-payment, one calculation activity, no Schedule, and carries both names as placeholders until their owner fixes them.
evidence: Context pack P8 'Jobs (2) JOB-07, JOB-08' and 'Workflows (0) None'; FSD P8 v3 A2.5.4.4 AC-BG-P8-005-01 'Payment matching / ACE batch for source ALS complete (v_ace_batch_status) / Daily'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-41 event FEE_DUE, R-DIS-10 event WORK_ORDER_RAISED, R-DIS-64 event BROKER_SOLD, R-WO-37 event PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the workflow platform owner (RWB-PLT-WF)
proposed: Name the fee run and its activity in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, and state in FSD P8 A2.5.2 whether the trigger is the fee-due event of the route owner or the daily batch completion; the story then replaces its placeholder and one of the two readings.
